newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ekran says listing won't hit KLSE - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ekran says listing won't hit KLSE - paper.

text.p: Ekran bhd Executive Chairman Ting Pek Khing has said the impending listing of Bakun Hydroel-Electric Corp (BHEC) would not destabilise the Malaysian market, the Star newspaper reported on Saturday.

"Some keep saying that we (BHEC) will have to raise eight billion ringgit from the public, that this will cause the market to collapse," the Star quoted Ting as saying in Miri, in Malaysia's Borneo state of Sarawak.
"This is not true. BHEC will attract public subscriptiuon of only 750 million ringgit. The rest of the 2.25 billion will come from major shareholders," Ting said.
BHEC plans to offer 1.5 billion shares at an initial offer price of two ringgit a share when it lists in June, in what would be one of Malaysia's biggest initial public offerings.
"We need only 750 million ringgit from the public," Ting said.
Earlier reports said that BHEC had originally proposed to raise 8 billion ringgit from the flotation, but this was subsequently scaled back to 3 billion ringgit.
BHEC is the operating company for the 13.6 billion ringgit-Bakun dam, which is under construction deep in a Sarawak rainforest.
The dam would create a reservoir the size of Singapore and clear 69,000 hectares of forest land. It is scheduled for completion by 2003.

Ekran would hold a 32 percent stake in BHEC and the Sarawak government and Sarawak Electricity Supply Corp 28 percent. Holding five percent each would be Tenaga Nasional Bhd, state-owned Khazanah Holdings and the national pension scheme Employees Provident Fund.
Ten percent of the shares would be sold to foreign investors and 15 percent to the Malaysian public.
Ting said BHEC expect to raise another 3 billion ringgit a year after the listing.
He said the federal government would back the the Bakun project by issuing a revolving guarantee for 500 million ringgit to pay the consortium building the 2,400-megawatt dam and power station.
Swiss-based ABB Asea Brown Boveri and Brazil's Companhia Braseileira de Projectos e Obras have been awarded the contract to design and build the dam and its transmission network.
"In fact, from the listing itself, we will have enough to pay the consortium. The project will be self-financing," Ting said.
